{{Short description|30th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1960–61 National Hurling League |image = |dates =23 October 1960 – 7 May 1961 |teams = |team1 = Tipperary |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 10th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |previous = [[1959–60 National Hurling League|1959–60]] |next = [[1961–62 National Hurling League|1961–62]] }} The '''1960–61 National Hurling League''' was the 30th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |image = |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1960-61 |winners=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]
10th National League title
Captain: [[Matt Hassett]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1959–60 National Hurling League|1959–60]] |nextseason=[[1961–62 National Hurling League|1961–62]] |updated=26 February 2017 }} [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1959-60 National Hurling League|1959-60 season]]. [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 7 May 1961, Tipperary won the title after a 6–6 to 4–9 win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.
